question: A permanent is an enchantment with a static ability saying it isn't a creature as long as your devotion to its color is less than five, and your devotion is currently two. A second enchantment then resolves whose static ability says every non-Aura enchantment you control is a creature with power and toughness each equal to its mana value. Is the first permanent a creature, and if so what are its power and toughness?
answer_gold: Yes, it is a creature, and its power and toughness are each equal to its mana value. Both type-changing effects apply in layer 4 and neither depends on the other, so they are applied in timestamp order (CR 613.1d, 613.7): the permanent's own effect removes the creature type first, then the later effect makes it a creature. The power/toughness-setting effect applies in layer 7b (CR 613.4b), after the type has already been settled.

question: You control a 2/2 creature with no abilities, and a permanent whose static ability says creatures with no abilities get +2/+2. A spell resolves giving that creature +1/+0 and first strike until end of turn. An opponent then resolves a permanent whose static ability says creatures they control have first strike and creatures you control can't have first strike. What are your creature's final power and toughness?
answer_gold: 5/4. In layer 6, the opponent's can't-have-first-strike effect prevents the spell from granting first strike to your creature (CR 613.1f), and the opponent's permanent grants your creature nothing, so your creature ends layer 6 with no abilities. In layer 7c it therefore receives +2/+2 from the no-abilities effect, and it still receives +1/+0 from the spell, because that spell's power/toughness part applies in layer 7c independently of whether its ability-granting part took effect.

question: You control a permanent that is both a land with a basic land type and a creature. An opponent resolves an effect saying creatures you control lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 1/1. Can you still tap that permanent for mana of the color its basic land type produces?
answer_gold: No. The mana ability is intrinsic to the basic land type rather than printed on the permanent (CR 305.6), but it is still an ability, so the lose-all-abilities effect removes it in layer 6 (CR 613.1f).

question: A continuous effect from a static ability says all nonland permanents are legendary. An effect then creates a token that is a copy of a legendary creature on the battlefield, and that copy effect specifies the token is not legendary. Once the token is on the battlefield, is it legendary?
answer_gold: Yes. The copy effect determines the token's copiable values, so the token is created without the legendary supertype. But the 'all nonland permanents are legendary' effect applies in layer 4 to every applicable object on the battlefield regardless of when that object entered (CR 613.1d), so it is applied on top of the copiable values and makes the token legendary.

question: A creature receives a flying counter. Later, an ability resolves that makes it lose flying for as long as that effect lasts. Later still, the creature receives a second flying counter. Then one of the two flying counters is removed from it. Does the creature have flying?
answer_gold: Yes. Keyword counters and ability-removing effects both apply in layer 6 and are applied in timestamp order (CR 613.1f). When the second flying counter was put on the creature, every flying counter already on it received a new timestamp identical to the new counter's (CR 613.7c), so the one remaining counter has a later timestamp than the lose-flying effect and is applied after it.

question: An Equipment is attached to a creature, and its static ability says the equipped creature loses flying. An Aura is then attached to that same creature, and its static ability says the enchanted creature has flying. Does the creature have flying?
answer_gold: Yes. Both effects apply in layer 6, and neither changes what the other applies to or does, so there is no dependency and they are applied in timestamp order (CR 613.3, 613.7). An Aura or Equipment receives a new timestamp each time it becomes attached (CR 613.7e), and the Aura was attached later, so its effect is applied last and wins.

question: A permanent's static ability says all creatures lose all abilities and have base power and toughness 1/1. A spell then resolves that puts a creature onto the battlefield and gives that creature haste until end of turn. Does that creature have haste?
answer_gold: Yes. Both effects apply in layer 6 and are applied in timestamp order (CR 613.1f, 613.7). The spell's effect was created when it resolved, so it has the later timestamp and is applied after the lose-all-abilities effect, which means the granted haste is not stripped.

question: A creature has a static ability making all cards and permanents a single chosen color. An opponent then resolves an enchantment whose static ability says all creatures lose all abilities. What color is the creature, and what color is the opponent's enchantment?
answer_gold: Both are the chosen color. The color-changing effect applies in layer 5 and the ability-removing effect applies in layer 6 (CR 613.1e, 613.1f). Because layer 5 is applied before layer 6, the color-changing effect has already been applied by the time the ability generating it is removed, and it continues to apply. The effect applies to all permanents, so the opponent's enchantment is that color too.
